turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am, I'll call Estella. Right away, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, I suppose, has failed to educate you in the art of playing the piano?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid not, ma'am, Estella has been kind enough to teach me a little, but I don't think I'm very good at it.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I demand to hear you play, immediately, and with some semblance of skill, or I shall be forced to dismiss you from my presence.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I'm not very good at playing the piano, ma'am, and I don't think it's proper for me to play in front of you and Estella

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: How dare you question my propriety, boy! I demand that you play for me, and do not bother to apologize, for it is beneath you to think that you might offend me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure, ma'am, I've never played in front of anyone before, and I don't know if I'd be any good.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I shall summon Estella to play for me, then. It is a small price to pay for your company, boy.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: If it's not too much trouble, ma'am, I'd rather not play if Estella is going to play too, I don't want to be in the way.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, come and play for us, my dear, I am not in the mood for this boy's excuses.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't know how to play any games, ma'am, I'm just a simple boy from the village.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You must play, boy, for I have grown weary of my own company. Your awkwardness will amuse me, perhaps even lift my spirits.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I'm not very good at playing games, ma'am, I'd rather just sit quietly and listen if that's all right with you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, do you think you can simply sit quietly and listen? I will not be entertained by your silence, I demand you play for me, at once!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I can do what you're asking, ma'am, I'm afraid I might make a mistake and get things wrong.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play, boy, and you will play now. Do not waste my time with your pitiful excuses.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm very sorry, Miss Havisham, but I don't know how to play any games that would please you, and I'm afraid I might break something in the house.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will not break anything that is mine, boy. I have been deceived and disappointed for far too long, and I will not be disappointed by you.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't wish to cause any trouble, Miss Havisham, but I'm afraid I'd rather not play just now, if it's all the same to you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play, boy, and you will play with Estella. It is for her benefit, and for mine.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
